newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends easier after hitting ceiling.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends easier after hitting ceiling.

text.p: July 7 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (H) 99.01 99.02
The key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures contract settled slightly easier on Monday after finding a solid ceiling.
"The current level is near the ceiling as it justifies no imminent rate rise," a long-term credit bank dealer said.
The contract rose as high as 99.04 earlier, retaining its firmness from last week. But it gave up the gains to settle down 0.01 at 99.01.
Turnover was a light 31,526 contracts.

"Those who bought on the fall in stocks in the morning sold this afternoon," the dealer said. "Further rises are unlikely unless the Nikkei falls below 19,500 or the dollar dips below 110 yen," he said.

The Nikkei ended at 19,705.17, down 262.83 points from Friday. The dollar briefly fell to 112.20 yen after Japan's trade data for the first 20 days of June showed a surplus of 453.20 billion yen, more than double that of a year earlier.
"Trade may stay directionless without new data on private demand for the July-September period," said a city bank dealer.

Meanwhile, concerns over Japan's bad loan problems revived after Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd, a medium-sized construction firm, applied for court protection on Friday, and this kept the downside room for the March limited, traders said.
"Fears remained that Japan's economic recovery may stall if other construction firms run into trouble," said a trust bank dealer.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate rose to around 0.50 percent on Monday from Friday's 0.45 percent, after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) less accommodative operation, traders said.
After the BOJ's drainage of 300 billion yen, instead of an expected drainage of 200 billion yen, the market was left with neither a surplus nor a shortfall.
It was the first time the BOJ had not left a surplus in the market since June 19. The BOJ has been leaving the market with a surplus of between 100 and 400 billion yen.

Traders said, however, the less-accommodative operation reflected good progress in banks' raising of funds and deposits for their quota with the BOJ in the current bank reserve period as well as the recent stabilisation in the long-end of the money market, and it was not a sign of higher interest rates.
The benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) rate fell to 0.67 percent by last Friday after hitting an 11-month high of 0.70 percent on July 1.
The three-month CDs were not issued on Monday, but were quoted at 0.72/0.67 percent, traders said.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, trade was subdued after sharp rate falls last week due to major domestic banks' aggressive buying of fixed interest rates.
The five-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.93/1.97 percent at 0730 GMT, against Friday's 1.89/1.93 percent.
-- Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
